image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Single support column of a pedestrian overpass standing on a road median, a square concrete plinth with chamfered top carrying a tall painted steel square-section column that ends in a short flat cross-beam with stiffener plates and bearing pads at both ends Materials: Green painted steel with chipped paint and rust bloom at the plinth junction, grey concrete plinth with soot and mud splash, yellow-black hazard stripes on the plinth, a faded advertising sticker on the column.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 556/8,000 triangles, 4/6 draw calls, 4/4 materials, 4/8 unique geometries, three canvases.

featureReviews.evidence: Built bounds -1.5..1.5, 0..5.5, -0.454..0.454 against the corrected 3.0 x 5.5 x 0.9; the pad tops at exactly 5.50 (an inner disc that overshot to 5.505 was replaced by a sole plate). check-coplanar clean.
I-beam with end plates, two discs on sole plates, base plate with four gussets, two head gussets, beads on the column faces, eight corner stripes.

Render clusters: #6e9b72 (142) 37%, #537153 (104) 25%, #163c1e (49) 26%, #898566 (132) 7% against the plate's steel 81 (shaded) and plinth 144; the lit column face probed at 137 against 122 before the 122/137 rescale.
featureReviews.notes: The 49 cluster is the bead shadow and the beam soffit: chromatic (sat 0.63), so clear of the neutral backdrop band.

name: Pedestrian Bridge Median Column
nameTh: เสาสะพานลอยกลางถนน
notes: Holds the walkway up over the centre of the road. MODULAR CONTRACT for the pedestrian set: pivot at ground (y=0), the bearing pads on the cross-beam top at y=5.5 so a span module placed with its pivot at y=5.5 sits on them; the cross-beam runs along X, 3 m long so it clears a 2.8 m span's width, and the column is 0.9 m along Z so two spans meeting over it at z=+-4 butt clear of it. Plinth 0.9 x 0.9 x 0.6, column 0.4 m square. No interior. DECLARATION CORRECTED 2026-09-09: the record read 0.9 x 5.5 x 3.0, which contradicts its own notes -- a 3 m cross-beam along X with a 0.9 m thickness along Z is a 3.0 x 5.5 x 0.9 envelope, and the span modules are the fixed side of the contract. Built bbox 3.000 x 5.500 x 0.908.
